messages:
anya: quick sync — i'm revisiting the idea of splitting the control plane surface for private customers. two modes i'm weighing: per-tenant vpc endpoints (pull model) vs shared regional relay (outbound-only tunnels). thoughts on long-term operability & security tradeoffs?

sam: high-level: per-tenant endpoints = stronger isolation, simpler routing for customer, but huge operational overhead (route tables, per-tenant ip mgmt, certs). relay = simpler infra but has a bigger blast radius and more complicated auth.

maria: +1. also watch egress/ip preservation. customers often need static egress IPs for allowlists — relay adds a NAT hop unless we preserve source (hard). SNAT scaling costs money.

anya: exactly. alternative: keep outbound-only tunnels from customer -> regional relay but provide per-customer egress mapping (one-to-one elastic ip per tenant) as a paid SKU. keeps infra simple, still meets customer needs. downside: ip scarcity and bookkeeping.

sam: question: how stateful do we allow the relay to be? i.e., should the relay hold active tenant routing entries (hot cache) or be completely stateless and forward based on token auth each request? stateful helps reduce auth latency but adds failure modes.

maria: lean toward stateless for control plane messages (auth each request). for streaming inference traffic, we might allow sticky tunnels with a short TTL cached per-connector. if a tunnel dies, fallback to a different relay.

anya: i sketched a connector lifecycle model: ephemeral-connector starts outbound TLS to regional relay with mTLS using customer-signed cert -> relay validates (OIDC + cert) -> relay issues short-lived session token for subsequent requests. pruning policy on idle connectors. snippet: \n\n```\nconnector_config = {\n  mode: "ephemeral",\n  keepalive_seconds: 30,\n  idle_ttl_seconds: 300,\n  reconnect_jitter: 30,\n  session_ttl_seconds: 900,\n}\n```\n\nsam: that looks reasonable. pruning heuristics: don't prune during active workflows (inference KV warmup), use a metric like recent_token_use_count > 0. also gradually increase idle_ttl for customers with high churn to avoid thrashing.

maria: operational concerns: updating cert chain and rotation if we rely on customer-signed certs. need an automated cert rotation path (operator API) and a migration plan for older agents. Also instrument connector counts per-relay and shard by customer size to avoid hotspot.

infra-bot: RFC: controlplane-connector-lifecycle-v2 merged into main at 2024-04-11 15:12 UTC :white_check_mark:

anya: good catch infra-bot. rollout plan thoughts: start with small customers on relay mode, monitor 95th latency, connection churn, and egress ip allocation metrics. have canary that pins 5 enterprise customers to per-tenant endpoints to validate isolation story.

sam: failure modes we need tests for: relay loss (how many customers impacted), certificate/key compromise, and route table drift if we use per-tenant endpoints. also simulate SNAT exhaustion to validate billing and mitigation.

maria: add operational playbooks: auto-failover to alternate region, and automated ip reclamation worker for stale egress allocations. for per-tenant endpoints we need a cleanup job that verifies route table entries and security group hygiene.

anya: one more idea: split control plane surface into two logical tiers: "management" (admin config, rollout control) and "inference control" (per-request routing, session tokens). management plane can be more strictly isolated per-customer, inference control can be regional and optimized for throughput. keeps the security boundary tight where it matters.

sam: i like that. management plane per-customer => stores keys/secrets and audits. inference plane regional => optimized runtime. need strong logging correlation IDs to trace sessions back to management actions.

maria: agree. action items:
- define connector pruning algorithm & default params (anya)
- design session token lifecycle + rotation & operator API for certs (sam)
- egress ip allocation policy + reclamation worker (maria)
- run chaos scenario tests for relay loss & SNAT exhaustion (eng-sre)

anya: i'll open issues for the first two today and assign owners. can we sync tomorrow 10am for a short design check? :calendar: 

sam: ack. i'll draft the session token spec and edge auth flow.

maria: ack, i'll prototype an allocation queue for egress ips and a reclamation lambda spike.

anya: thanks all. keeping this lightweight — thread closed unless folks have follow-ups. :pray:
